title: Inca — 5yo alpaca: weakness and very pale gums two weeks after arriving
presentation: 5-year-old female alpaca, bought in a fortnight ago from a dispersal sale. Lagging behind the herd, weak, gums almost white, and she has lost condition since arrival.

stages.title: Examine the alpaca
stages.briefing: BCS 2/5. Mucous membranes almost white, HR 96 bpm, RR 40/min, temperature 39.3°C. Weak, reluctant to rise. No bottle jaw, no external bleeding, faeces normal. Fleece dull. Bought at a dispersal sale two weeks ago, transported 200 miles, mixed into a group of twelve, mild shearing wound on the flank now healed.

options.label: Severe pallor with tachycardia and tachypnoea
options.detail: Anaemia sufficient to compromise oxygen delivery

options.label: Recent purchase, transport and mixing
options.detail: Stress that unmasks latent infection in camelids

options.label: Fever of 39.3°C with the anaemia
options.detail: Points to an infectious or immune cause rather than blood loss

options.label: Absence of bottle jaw
options.detail: Useful — it argues against heavy Haemonchus — but it is a negative

options.label: Healed shearing wound
options.detail: No longer a source of blood loss

stages.explanation: Anaemia with fever and no evidence of blood loss puts destruction ahead of haemorrhage, and in a recently purchased, transported camelid the organism at the top of that list is Mycoplasma haemolamae, which lives latently and flares under stress. The absent bottle jaw is worth noting because Haemonchus is the other great camelid anaemia and is treated entirely differently.

stages.title: Choose the tests
stages.briefing: You can take blood in the field and submit samples to a laboratory that offers camelid PCR.

options.label: Packed cell volume and total protein
options.detail: Grades the anaemia and separates protein loss

options.label: Blood smear examined for organisms on the red cell surface
options.detail: M. haemolamae is seen, if you look before treatment

options.label: Mycoplasma haemolamae PCR
options.detail: More sensitive than the smear, which is often negative

options.label: Faecal egg count
options.detail: Haemonchus is the other cause of camelid anaemia

options.label: Reticulocyte or new methylene blue stain for regeneration
options.detail: Regenerative or not shapes the prognosis

options.label: Coombs test as the first-line test
options.detail: Poorly validated in camelids and it would not change today

options.label: Bone marrow aspirate before simpler tests
options.detail: Invasive, and unnecessary if the PCR is positive

stages.explanation: A blood smear costs nothing and can be diagnostic, but M. haemolamae is famously intermittent on smears, so the PCR is what confirms it — and both need taking before any oxytetracycline is given. A faecal count runs in parallel because the two diseases coexist, and in a thin alpaca you want to know about both before you decide the anaemia is explained.

stages.title: Interpret the results
stages.briefing: PCV 11% (ref 27–45), total protein 62 g/L (ref 55–75), albumin 32 g/L. Blood smear: occasional small basophilic organisms on the red cell margins; marked anisocytosis. M. haemolamae PCR strongly positive. Faecal egg count 200 epg strongyle-type, no Haemonchus predominance on speciation. New methylene blue: reticulocytosis present. Total bilirubin mildly raised. Two herd mates: PCV 26% and 31%, both PCR positive, clinically well.
stages.prompt: Which conclusions do these results support?

options.label: Regenerative haemolytic anaemia from Mycoplasma haemolamae
options.detail: PCR positive with organisms on the smear and reticulocytosis

options.label: The herd carries the organism subclinically
options.detail: Two well herd mates PCR positive

options.label: Parasitism is not the main cause of this anaemia
options.detail: A count of 200 epg with normal protein

options.label: Haemonchosis is the primary diagnosis
options.detail: Low count, no Haemonchus predominance, and protein is normal

options.label: Non-regenerative anaemia of chronic disease
options.detail: Reticulocytosis says the marrow is responding

stages.explanation: Normal total protein is what takes Haemonchus off the top of the list — a parasite that sucks blood takes albumin with it. The positive PCRs in two healthy herd mates are the finding that reframes the case: this is a latent herd infection in which one stressed animal has decompensated, so the plan covers the individual and the management of the group, not mass treatment of well animals.

stages.title: Commit to a diagnosis
stages.briefing: PCV 11% with normal protein, regenerative response, organisms on the smear, M. haemolamae PCR strongly positive, low strongyle count, two PCR-positive healthy herd mates.

options.label: Mycoplasma haemolamae anaemia, flared by the stress of purchase and transport
options.detail: Confirmed organism, regenerative anaemia, recognised trigger

options.label: Haemonchosis
options.detail: Normal protein and a low egg count

options.label: Immune-mediated haemolytic anaemia
options.detail: Possible in camelids, but the PCR names an infectious cause

options.label: Copper deficiency
options.detail: Would not give a fever or a positive PCR

options.label: Blood loss from the shearing wound
options.detail: Healed, and blood loss would lower the protein

stages.explanation: Naming the stress trigger is what makes the herd advice concrete: oxytetracycline and supportive care for this alpaca, and for the group, quarantine and minimising stress at purchase rather than blanket treatment. Camelids carry this organism for life, so the goal is preventing the next flare, not clearing the herd.
